extraction.name: Cleaned YODAS Dataset (OWSM v4)
extraction.description: A cleaned subset of the YODAS (Youtube-Oriented Dataset for Audio and Speech) dataset, processed through a scalable data-cleaning pipeline. The resulting dataset contains 166,000 hours of speech across 75 languages, created by applying resegmentation, language identification-based filtering, and CTC-score-based filtering to the raw YODAS data. This dataset is used to train the OWSM v4 series of open speech foundation models supporting multilingual ASR, speech translation, and language identification.
extraction.creator: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe
extraction.publisher: Carnegie Mellon University; Honda Research Institute Japan
extraction.citeAs: Peng, Y., Shakeel, M., Sudo, Y., Chen, W., Tian, J., Lin, C.-J., & Watanabe, S. (2025). OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning. Proc. Interspeech 2025, 17-21 August 2025, Rotterdam, The Netherlands. doi:10.21437/Interspeech.2025-1062
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from YODAS (Youtube-Oriented Dataset for Audio and Speech), a large-scale web-crawled dataset. YODAS provides unsegmented long-form audio recordings with text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps. The raw YODAS data includes 370k hours of audio in 149 languages. A scalable data-cleaning pipeline was applied to produce the final 166k hours across 75 languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The raw YODAS data contains incorrect language labels and audio-text misalignments. When no CTC-score filtering is applied (θCTC=0.00), performance on Common Voice is poor and unstable, with decoding often getting stuck in repetitions, leading to WERs exceeding 100%, confirming substantial misalignment issues in the raw data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source is YODAS (Youtube-Oriented Dataset for Audio and Speech), which includes 370k hours of audio in 149 languages crawled from the web (YouTube). YODAS publicly releases audio files under a Creative Commons license and provides unsegmented long-form audio recordings with text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The data-cleaning pipeline consists of three steps: (1) Resegmentation: audio and text are realigned using the CTC segmentation algorithm with the publicly available OWSM-CTC v3.2 model. Long-form recordings are segmented into shorter utterances with a maximum duration of 30 seconds. Utterances consisting exclusively of non-speech elements (e.g., music) are removed. This yields 345k hours across 83 languages. (2) LID-based filtering: Language identification is performed on both audio and text using fastText (text-based LID) and ECAPA-TDNN via SpeechBrain (spoken LID). Only utterances where the original language label matches both predicted languages are retained, yielding 284k hours across 75 languages. (3) CTC-score-based filtering: Utterances with low-quality audio-text alignments are removed based on CTC confidence scores. A relative threshold (quantile) θCTC=0.10 is applied per language; long-form utterances containing any short utterance in the lowest θCTC quantile are discarded, yielding the final 166k hours across 75 languages.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Three-step pipeline: (1) Resegmentation using CTC segmentation algorithm with OWSM-CTC v3.2 to realign audio and text, segment into ≤30s utterances, and remove non-speech utterances. (2) LID-based filtering using fastText (text LID) and ECAPA-TDNN/SpeechBrain (audio LID) to remove utterances with mismatched language labels. (3) CTC-score-based filtering with threshold θCTC=0.10 to remove utterances with low audio-text alignment quality. The threshold was selected by fine-tuning OWSM v3.1 small on data filtered at varying thresholds and evaluating on Common Voice and a web presentation corpus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset uses existing transcriptions from YODAS, which were originally annotated with start and end timestamps. These annotations were realigned using the CTC segmentation algorithm with the OWSM-CTC v3.2 model to improve accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: ESPnet toolkit; OWSM-CTC v3.2 model (https://huggingface.co/espnet/owsm_ctcv3.2_ft1B); fastText language identification (https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html); SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN (https://huggingface.co/speechbrain/lang-id-voxlingua107-ecapa)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: CTC confidence scores are used to quantify alignment quality between audio and text. Scores are language-dependent, so relative thresholds (quantiles) are applied per language. Different threshold values yield varying amounts of retained data. The threshold θCTC=0.10 was selected as it retains the majority of data while providing generally good performance across languages.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OWSM-CTC v3.2 (CTC segmentation and confidence scoring), fastText (text-based language identification), ECAPA-TDNN via SpeechBrain (spoken language identification)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The cleaned YODAS data, pre-trained models, training code, and all associated scripts will be publicly released via the ESPnet toolkit. Training logs will also be released.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and associated models advance open academic research in multilingual speech processing by providing a fully open alternative to proprietary speech foundation models like Whisper. The work supports transparency, reproducibility, and accessibility in speech AI research across 75 languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The distribution across languages is highly imbalanced, similar to the raw YODAS data. English constitutes the largest share (74.6k hours out of 166k total at θCTC=0.10), while many other languages remain underrepresented. The original distribution is kept without any resampling.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The language distribution is highly imbalanced with English dominating. The OWSM-CTC v3.2 model used for resegmentation supports only a subset of the languages present in YODAS, limiting coverage. The dataset retains some noise as the θCTC=0.10 threshold is a compromise between data quantity and quality.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and fine-tuning speech foundation models for multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR), speech translation (ST), and spoken language identification (LID). The dataset is used to train the OWSM v4 series of models supporting these tasks across 75 languages.
